_comment: Transit operations, tariffs and carbon factors. Each block carries provenance with a verification_status. Nothing is presented as verified unless a published source was located and read.

sources_consulted: TNERC Suo-motu Order No. 6 of 2023, dated 30-06-2023, effective 01-07-2023 (Tariff for Distribution FY 2023-24), clause 3.1.7 High Tension Tariff V - Public EV Charging Stations (explicitly covers battery swapping)
CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, Version 20 (Dec 2024); User Guide v21
Gelera-Adefuin, M.J. (2019) IJITEE v8(6) - Ukkadam Lake water quality survey (n=14)
Nept Journal - Monitoring the Pollution Intensity of Wetlands of Coimbatore
NASA POWER API v2.10.0 point query, 10.99N 76.96E, 2023
provenance.honesty_note: Blocks marked verification_status='assumption' are inherited project assumptions with no confirmed primary source. They must not be cited as measured values.

provenance.note: 220 km/day is a plausible city-bus duty cycle but was not confirmed against a TNSTC published per-vehicle figure; the corporation figure of 10.81 lakh km/day spans intercity, hilly and town operations and cannot be divided by fleet size to give a city-bus duty cycle. The diesel price is an approximate retail figure for the period, not a dated IOCL bulletin. Treat the assumption group as editable.

transit_operations.corridor_archetypes_note: Illustrative demand archetypes used only to vet tariff and energy arithmetic. They are NOT the simulated network geometry, which lives in src/config/settings.py as Route 69/1/2/3 (standard) and Route 45/70 (expanded).

verified_operations_reference.electric_bus_programme: KfW-funded procurement of 12,000 BS-VI and 2,000 electric buses; 500 electric buses for Chennai, Madurai and Coimbatore, with 100 e-buses in the first phase.

sources: TNSTC (Coimbatore) Ltd RTI handbook, tn.gov.in (fleet strength and daily KMs as on 31.10.2025)
The Times of India, 13 Apr 2022, 'TNSTC Coimbatore division saves more than 3,300 litres of diesel daily' (city mileage ~5.10 KMPL, rural 5.57 KMPL)
Government of Tamil Nadu, Economic Review 2022-23, Transport Department (state STU fuel performance 5.33 KMPL average, 2021-22)
provenance.correction_note: The earlier draft used 3.5 km/L, which is well below the published TNSTC Coimbatore city figure of ~5.10 KMPL and appears to be a generic fleet figure rather than a Coimbatore measurement. Using 3.5 overstated daily diesel burn by ~46% (62.86 L vs 43.14 L per bus).

electricity_tariffs.order_reference: TNERC Suo-motu Order No. 6 of 2023, effective 01-07-2023
electricity_tariffs.applicable_category: HT-V Public EV Charging Station (includes battery-swapping stations)

provenance.source: TNERC Suo-motu Order No. 6 of 2023, dated 30-06-2023, effective 01-07-2023 (Tariff for Distribution FY 2023-24), clause 3.1.7 High Tension Tariff V - Public EV Charging Stations (explicitly covers battery swapping)
provenance.units: commission-determined energy charges in paise/kWh (600 / 900 / 750) converted to Rs/kWh
provenance.correction_note: An earlier draft carried 6.50 / 9.75 / 8.10. Those rates do not appear in TNERC Order No. 6 of 2023 and are corrected here to the published 6.00 / 9.00 / 7.50.

secondary_assumptions_provenance.note: The 8.00 base commercial rate and 0.54 open-access surcharge are inherited project assumptions driving the simulated mode. Not re-verified against the current TANGEDCO schedule; confirm before external citation.

provenance.source: CEA CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, Version 20 (Dec 2024); User Guide v21
provenance.unit_note: CEA publishes tCO2/MWh, numerically identical to kgCO2/kWh.
provenance.series_note: Weighted-average grid emission factor including renewable generation.
provenance.correction_note: An earlier draft recorded 0.823 for 2022-23. The CEA series gives 0.716; corrected.

diesel_factor_provenance.note: 2.68 kgCO2/L is the conventional stoichiometric diesel combustion factor.
